page.layout: One printed page, one text block in a single column with marginal notes on the right. Running head at top, page number at top right. Below the text, a gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.l: nũ[?] Plato de Republ. lib.7. & Epinomide; &
Aristot.de coelo & mundo, & in libro de me-
chanicis artibus, quas ita ex Geometria ducit,
& praeterea Cicero de natura Deorum 2. & de
universitate, & in somnio Scipionis, & in Ara-
to converso: sed in primis principes ipsi Euclides,
Ptolemaeus, Higynus, & alii. De his vide & li-
XII. LITERÆ deinde illæ, quæ quasvis hu-
jusmodi literas attingunt, & non tàm in gene-
rali speculatione versantur, quàm in exemplis,
sunt poësis, historia & oratoria facultas: unde

l.i: major deinde rerum & verborum copia nascitur. In-
primis autem hic Græci & Latini autores cognoscendi.

main_text.l: 1. Historia autem res veras sicut gesta sunt aut
2. Poësis res plerunq; fingit, aut fabularum in-

l.i: volucris tegit. Vide Platonem in Ione, & Ciceronem
pro Archia, & Plutarchum de legendis poëtis, & de
Homeri vita & librorum ejus interpretatione, & Ba-
nis vi & copia, res persequitur. Sed Instrumenta illa,
licet nulla sint, sine materia rerum & verborum,
quam tractent: tamen commodissimum est illa parata
habere: eamq; ob causam primum etiam
traduntur, & Plato, ut dixi, παιδείαν[?] vocat.

page.notes: Printed text is in one column; the only marginal notes are "Historia.", "Poësis." and "Oratoria." on the right. The first word of the page is a fragment (the line begins with a damaged abbreviation before "Plato"), transcribed as "nũ[?]". The Greek word "παιδείαν" at the end is set in a worn type and is uncertain. The signature "r 5" at the foot is read from a faint mark. No catchword is visible. Printed spellings such as "tàm", "quàm", "Inprimis" and "plerunq;" are kept as printed.
